subject: Executive SLA alert: transit flapping causing elevated 5xx and token latency
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna@orbitpay.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos@orbitpay.com>, noc@orbitpay.com
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx + token latency starting ~08:50 UTC - urgent

Hi Lauren,

Sorry to bother you early — OrbitPay is seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors from Redwood endpoints starting ~08:50 UTC today. Error rates jumped from <0.1% to ~6% and median token latency increased from 120ms to ~800ms. Throughput dropped intermittently (we're seeing large retry loops on our side).

We validated locally: a small subset of requests are returning 502 and 504; others time out after multiple TCP retries. Our application traces show the requests lost <trace-ids: op-8f3a, op-8f3b>. We've already opened a pager with our cloud provider — they see anomalous BGP churn on one of their transit peers.

Can you confirm whether this is on your routing/proxy side? This is affecting our checkout flow — we need an ETA for mitigation and whether this qualifies for SLA credit.

Thanks,
Jenna
SRE, OrbitPay

Attachments: small-sample-traces.txt (3 traces)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@orbitpay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, noc@orbitpay.com
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx + token latency starting ~08:50 UTC - urgent

Hi Jenna — thanks for the alert and the sample traces. I'm escalating immediately.

Internal team (Marcus, Naomi): please confirm whether we're seeing VPC peering or resolver symptoms from our side. Initial ask: 1) confirm if a Redwood edge or our proxy cluster is returning 502/504s at scale, 2) share any recent ACL/ASN changes, and 3) push quick mitigations if we can (route pinning / fallback to alternate resolver / bypass proxy).

OrbitPay: we'll keep you in the loop and propose an action plan in the next 30 minutes. If this is a transit BGP issue upstream, we'll coordinate a short mitigation (traffic steering) and follow with a postmortem.

Lauren
Director, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx + token latency starting ~08:50 UTC - urgent

Lauren/Team — quick update from the network side:

What we see:
- Starting 08:48 UTC there are multiple short-duration flaps on the peering session between us-east-1 transit hop (AS64501) and upstream transit provider.
- Some traffic is being rerouted through a legacy Anycast resolver that returns an older proxy VIP. That proxy cluster has a rate-limit/worker saturation pattern that causes 502s and client-visible timeouts.
- Our edge probes show increased TCP retransmits and SYN retries (~3x baseline) during the windows Jenna observed.

Immediate findings: hdr-trace attached (hdr-trace-20280901.pcap) — shows TCP handshake loops to proxy VIP 52.14.77.9 and a couple of long resolver lookups that fall back to 504.

Short-term mitigation we initiated (10:05 UTC):
1) Pin affected customer traffic to secondary egress (us-east-1-b) for OrbitPay using traffic steering rule TS-ORBIT-01.
2) Bypass the legacy resolver for OrbitPay routes by adding forced DNS resolution to our local forwarding cache for the customer domain.
3) Increase proxy worker pool temporarily for the impacted VIP.

I recommend holding the customer traffic on the pinned route for 60–90 minutes while we monitor. If the upstream transit stabilizes we can rollback.

I will keep the pcap and a slowpath CSV (slowpath-summary-20280901.csv) in the incident folder.

-Marcus
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx + token latency starting ~08:50 UTC - urgent

Added a few datapoints:
- DNS shows intermittent resolution to 52.14.77.9 (legacy VIP) and 34.201.11.12 (current VIP). The event is correlated with upstream Anycast shift that prefers a legacy PoP for some prefixes.
- Customer-side NAT sessions were hitting an ACL change window (OrbitPay had a rolling change at 08:40 UTC per their change log) which likely increased session churn as the path moved.

Suggested next steps:
- Recommend OrbitPay rollback the change or hold sessions while we keep traffic pinned.
- Post-incident: we'll add a short runbook to disable Anycast fallback for user-critical VIPs and add an automatic health weight to avoid legacy proxies.

Naomi
Platform Ops

Date: Sun, 03 Sep 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: OrbitPay incident summary and exec next steps (SLA/credits & remediation)

Jenna/Carlos — thank you for your patience while we worked through this. Below is an executive summary and immediate next steps.

Summary (what happened):
- 08:48–09:15 UTC 2028-09-01: An upstream transit peer experienced short BGP churn that shifted a subset of traffic to a legacy Anycast PoP. That PoP routed requests to a legacy proxy VIP which had limited worker capacity, resulting in elevated 502/504 rates and token latency spikes.
- Contributing factor: OrbitPay performed a rolling ACL change ~08:40 UTC which increased NAT session churn and amplified client retries during the transit instability window.

Actions taken (what we did):
- Traffic steering to secondary egress (TS-ORBIT-01) and forced DNS pinning for OrbitPay traffic.
- Increased proxy worker pool for impacted VIP and added temporary health weighting to avoid legacy PoP.
- Collected full packet captures and slowpath traces (attached).

Current state:
- Errors returned to baseline by 10:30 UTC after the steering and temporary mitigations. No further customer impact detected since rollback window.

Next steps and asks:
1) OrbitPay: please consider rolling back the ACL change during a maintenance window if you need to reapply. That will reduce session churn risk while we test runbook changes.
2) Redwood (Network): create a short postmortem and follow-through for: a) disable Anycast fallback for critical proxy VIPs, b) automatic weighting to avoid legacy PoPs, c) improved egress failover playbook.
3) Exec (Vivek + Evelyn): recommend we approve a small one-time credit for OrbitPay (estimated 3% of last month usage) to acknowledge SLA impact — happy to finalize if you think different.

I'll schedule a 30-minute post-incident call tomorrow to walk through the details with OrbitPay and engineering.

Lauren
Director, Customer Success
